h33-h33-2-b2-MASSr10minus-20261023-6d3dd.hypothesis: R0 carries dead mass. The 37,654-dot Poisson-disk thinning of H19-5 at 2.8 px was selected for SPACING, not for evidence, so roughly a tenth of those dots sit on aeromagnetic ridge crests that no independent physical channel corroborates. Deleting the 3,765 dots whose removal costs the least kernel credit T while still removing one unit of mass S raises DTI, because DTI = T / (0.2T + 0.2(S-M) + 0.8|G|) penalises every emitted dot through S whether or not it lands on a fault.
h33-h33-2-b2-MASSr10minus-20261023-6d3dd.mechanism: Under the 300 m triangular kernel a dot only pays if its credit exceeds 0.2*DTI (about 0.056 at DTI 0.28). Dots that (a) already lie within 300 m of a stronger neighbour on the same strand, or (b) sit on a ridge that the TMI horizontal-gradient, isostatic-gravity gradient, and GDR-1391 geothermometry channels all fail to support, contribute S but almost no T. Removing them shrinks the denominator 0.2(T + S - M) + 0.8|G| immediately and shrinks T only by the third-order residual credit they uniquely held.
h33-h33-2-b2-MASSr10minus-20261023-6d3dd.non_fault_mimic: The corroboration field w is built from potential-field and topographic derivatives. A genuine but deeply buried, low-offset, or sediment-masked fault carries a weak magnetic and gravity expression, and 400 m GeoDAWN flight-line spacing (Area 2) can place its ridge crest up to a kernel radius off the true trace. Pruning 'low-w' dots therefore preferentially deletes blind and low-slip faults — precisely the population most likely to be in the new-fault label set — so a live score DROP is the expected outcome if w is a poor fault detector rather than a good one.

Every un-emitted H19-5 pixel survived the 2.8 px dot-thinning, which means it lies within 280 m of an already-emitted dot — inside the 300 m triangular kernel that already credits that strand — so a new dot there raises S by one and T by almost nothing, and DTI falls.

Once a strand is sampled every 280 m, the marginal dot on that strand has near-zero dT. The exact marginal-gain greedy therefore spends its 3,765 additions on whatever residual w it can still find — strand tips, step-over gaps, and low-w flanks — and the mean dT per added dot is the direct measurement of how saturated the parent field is.

If those carry real new-fault labels, additions pay. Conversely, ridge crests produced by flight-line levelling artefacts, drainage incision, and lithologic contacts are also in the pool and pay nothing, so the arm conflates 'add coverage' with 'add ridge artefacts'.
